parsed.explanation: Primary exposure is the enforced religious gender-expression offence criminalising cross-dressing/posing; it reaches visitors whose documents cannot match presentation. A 2014 conviction and reported enforcement of morality provisions show it is not dead letter, although 2017 had no known convictions and the code applies mainly to Muslims. Same-sex death/stoning provisions are tangential but severe, under a revocable moratorium; no border-screening or custody/recourse evidence exists, so unknowns weigh lightly and do not establish safety. State hostility, no independent rights monitoring, and inability to change documents raise risk. This is high, not severe: no documented recurring visitor raids or custody abuses, and no executions, keep it above the severe-risk anchors.
